sections.title: A second way to name the owner
sections.content: You already say "Péter's car" by putting the owner next to the possessed noun: *Péter autója*. There is a longer pattern that puts *-nak/-nek* on the owner and *a/az* before the possessed noun: *Péternek az autója*. The possessed noun keeps its own *-a/-e/-ja/-je*. You need the longer pattern when the owner is a question word (*kinek a ...?* "whose ...?") or has *ez/az* in front (*annak a fiúnak a kutyája* "that boy's dog"). With a plain name or noun, both patterns work.

items.spanish: Annak a fiúnak a kutyája nagyon hangos.
items.english: That boy's dog is very loud.

sections.content: *-nak* follows back vowels and *-nek* follows front vowels, as always: *fiúnak*, *Péternek*. A final *-a* or *-e* lengthens (*Anna* → *Annának*).
